turn.student: כמה זמן אפשר לשמור ביצים במקרר?

conceptsMissing: יצורים זעירים שגדלים ומתרבים על הלחם וניזונים ממנו

turns.text:
המסמך שלנו לא עוסק במשך הזמן המדויק שבו אפשר לשמור ביצים במקרר. כמידע כללי שאינו מופיע במסמך, בדרך כלל ביצים מחזיקות מעמד במקרר במשך מספר שבועות.

בוא נחזור לשאלה שלנו על מה שקורה במטבח: למה על לחם שנשאר כמה ימים בשקית מופיעים פתאום כתמים ירוקים?

turn.student: Magnets attract only a few materials. Iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are pulled by a magnet. Most other materials, including many metals such as aluminium, copper, gold and silver, are not attracted at all.

conceptsShown: magnets attract only a few materials like iron and steel
aluminium is not attracted by magnets
conceptsMissing: explains how the magnet separates the steel cans from the aluminium cans in the recycling plant

turns.text:
You got the part right that magnets attract materials like steel, but not aluminium [c2]. 

Now, imagine you have a pile of mixed cans. If you pass a big magnet right over the pile, which cans will actually jump up and stick to the magnet, and which ones will stay on the belt?

turn.student: The steel cans have iron in them so the magnet grabs them, and aluminium just isn't a magnetic metal, so those cans are left.

conceptsShown: steel cans contain iron and are pulled by the magnet
aluminium is not a magnetic metal and stays behind

turns.text:
You correctly identified that steel cans contain iron so the magnet grabs them, while aluminium is not a magnetic metal and is left behind. 

Did you know that the Earth you are standing on actually behaves like a giant magnet [c4]? A compass contains a tiny, light needle that can turn freely, and that needle is a small magnet itself [c4]. Because opposite poles attract, this little needle feels the invisible magnetic pull of the Earth and lines up with it [c4]. 

Why does a compass needle always point north?

turn.student: Because in December Australia is closer to the Sun than Europe is.

label.misconception: seasons come from distance to the Sun

turns.misconception: Thinking that summer and winter are caused by differences in distance from the Sun.

conceptsMissing: opposite seasons show distance is not the cause
assessment.misconception: Thinking that summer and winter are caused by differences in distance from the Sun.

turns.text:
Let's take a quick step back and look at how summer works. When your half of Earth is tilted towards the Sun, sunlight hits the ground more directly—like a flashlight shining straight down on a small spot instead of at an angle [c2]. That direct light and the longer days give the ground more time to warm up [c3]. 

So, when your part of Earth is having summer, is your half tilted towards or away from the Sun?
